auto_merge.commit_message:
Allows cython to understand ellipses as tuple subscript. Also, the level of warnings is increased to show the user when the subscript types are ignored.

---------

Co-authored-by: scoder <stefan_ml@behnel.de>

repo.description: The most widely used Python to C compiler
repo.name: cython

body:
Allows cython to understand ellipses as tuple subscript. Currently, this PR does not allow `tuple[...]` which should be allowed but usage is limited because it means tuple with one Ellipsis element inside.

This PR also increases level of warnings to show the user when subscript types are ignored.

comment_data.body: Following declarations are producing warnings but they are not asserted against `_WARNINGS`. Not sure why though...
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -237,6 +238,22 @@ def invalid_type_count():
     dict1: dict[int]
     dict2: dict[int, int, int]
 
+def invalid_ellipsis():

comment_data.body:
I don't think this is right.

This also also implies that 
1. `...()` produces an ellipsis instance.
2. `def f(x: ...)` is a function accepting an ellipsis instance (I think `None` is the only thing special-cased like that in the typing system)

     def compile_time_value(self, denv):

comment_data.body: Yeah I think you are right. `...` is an instance not a type. Hmm hence the handling of annotation must be aware that annotation is not only containing types but also `Node`s. I will try to craft something (hopefully) smart.

Main features:
- Pattern matching
- Generics / subscripted container types
- `@cython.collection_type()`
- `restrict`
- more vectorcalls
- more thread safety
- smaller modules, more shared code
- remove Py3.8 support, keep Py3.9+
